title: Last Chance
paragraphs: Last chance. That’s right—after my Older Sister came to get me from a parallel world, I was abandoned following a string of failures, and I was told point-blank that I’d never see Filo-chan again. My Older Sister gave me one last chance, as if it were an act of mercy. When I think back on that time, there are rare moments when I find myself wondering if I should show a little mercy to those who are hoping for a chance.
“Huh…”
“If I hadn’t managed to make the most of that chance, I might have wandered around forever without ever seeing Filo-chan again.”
“Aren’t you still unable to see her?”
“Gwaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
Father, how can you say such a merciless thing!? Oh, what on earth must I do to meet Filo-tan in this world!? Older Sister from the first world! Please, guide me to Filo-tan!

“Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan, Filo-tan!”
“Motoyasu-sama! Please calm down!”
“Sorry, that just slipped out. Motoyasu-kun, calm down! It was my fault—come back! Look, it’s Sakura-chan.”
Father picks up Sakura-chan, who had been sitting and resting, and holds her out to me.
“Hmm?”
“Filo-chan… Father, Sakura-chan isn’t Filo-chan. Sakura-chan is Sakura-chan.”
“I think it’s good that you snapped back to your senses so quickly, but you really are a handful, Motoyasu-kun…”
“You sure do do a lot of skits, don’t you…”
“It’s practically a running joke by now… Oh well. I guess this is just Motoyasu-kun being his usual self.”
Father sat Sakura-chan back down, then turned around and faced me.
“Anyway, I guess this means Motoyasu-kun is growing up. I was on the edge of my seat, worried he might propose a merciless massacre.”
“That’s a different matter entirely.”
If he were to disregard my mercy, then it would truly be time for “Destroy.” I’ll make him pay just like I did to Takt and the Three Heroes Church.

“What…? If I got serious and started firing off a barrage of Liberation Firestorm X and the like, I could turn a country of this size into a wasteland in the blink of an eye. Or perhaps I should try a test firing of the Liberation Meltblast, which is currently under development?”
It’s a wide-area annihilation Magic with its power boosted to the absolute limit. It’s just the thing for sweeping away this rabble.
“I’m hearing some ominous-sounding Magic names here… firing massive beams from your eyes, casually talking about turning a country into a wasteland…”
“Want me to give it a try?”
“No need.”
Father, who looks rather exhausted, orders me around. What a shame.
“Anyway, I was prepared for this even before coming to Shieldfreeden. Things are about to get tough, so this is where we’ll really have to hold our ground.”
I suppose so. Since it’s a country under Takt’s influence, it’s only natural that it’s a mess. That said, surprisingly, Father was quite assertive today.
“You seemed pretty assertive today, Father—perhaps because you’re focused on making improvements?”
“Ah… well, yeah. If I just let it slide by saying, ‘Oh well, terrorists showed up there, so it can’t be helped,’ that’d play right into their hands.”
“Is something going on?”
“How should I put it? The fact that the representatives of the defeated nation didn’t come to greet us at the airport makes me suspicious.”

Hmm, it’s true that they were waiting at the castle. I assumed that’s just how things are, but given the current relationship between Siltvelt and Shieldfreeden, that response might be a bit unnatural. Father must be thinking that it wouldn’t be strange if terrorists showed up—or that they’re somehow connected. That’s precisely why he’s resolving the situation first, then barging in and taking a high-handed approach. I suppose he figures it would be worse to back down now and let them get the upper hand.
“Well, it’ll be interesting to see if the Shield Hero can pull off being a politician.”
“If anything, I plan to leave that sort of thing to the people of Siltvelt. Our goal is to eradicate the waves and the Takt faction, which pose a threat.”
“That’s why you came here, wasn’t it? With that sudden welcome, I actually started wondering how you were going to change the country.”
“Well… I might have a little say in the matter. Well then, let’s rest until the meeting and get ready to take on the challenge.”
And so, after taking a short break, we ended up having a meeting with the people of Shieldfreeden.

The people of Shieldfreeden escorted Father and me to the conference room, and we took our seats for the meeting. Since it was decided that it would be more effective for me to remain silent as much as possible, Father took charge of giving instructions on our policy and other matters.
“Um… Shield Hero, regarding your inspection tour of Shieldfreeden, we’d like to host the warmest welcome and parade possible—what do you think?”
“I think it’s necessary for the triumphant return of a victorious nation.”
Not only the people of Shieldfreeden, but those from Siltvelt are making the same proposal as well. A parade, huh? This would be a great opportunity to showcase Father’s prestige.
“Didn’t you already do that on the way here?”
“That was just to get you here… If we go through with it, we’ll make it much more grand.”
A parade to welcome Father, then! I’m getting excited. Let’s make it as grand as when we saved the first world.

“From the perspective of someone who was shot at the bridge of the nose right after arriving in this country, I’d like to postpone it. There’s even a possibility that poison could be mixed into our food indiscriminately. They’ll likely use our arrival as an excuse to blame these incidents on us. It’s fine to push ahead, but it shouldn’t be too late to wait and see how things develop a bit longer.”
“Understood. The Hero’s point is well taken. Let’s hold off on the parade and such until things have settled down.”
The first agenda item was quickly postponed. It’s a shame, but it looks like the parade isn’t happening after all.
“So, what about Nelshen—was that his name? The former representative, the Aotatsu of the Takt faction, and the president of Shieldfreeden—what’s the latest on his whereabouts?”

“Um… To explain the details, when the Shieldfreeden army advanced into Siltvelt, he was in the rear, serving as the operations officer. However, the heroes destroyed their aircraft and other weapons, and the army suffered a devastating blow, forcing a retreat… After returning to their home country, he suddenly vanished.”
“He must have realized they’d lost the war and gone into hiding.”

That’s quite the pig-like getaway. Isn’t that a run for it on par with a Lazy Pig? No… a Lazy Pig immediately senses any trouble and escapes out of my range, so this is probably even worse. That creature’s ability to avoid danger is nothing short of divine.
“Have you determined whether he left Shieldfreeden?”
“We’re conducting strict checkpoints throughout the region, but he doesn’t seem to be getting caught.”
“Even so… aren’t the ones manning the checkpoints from Shieldfreeden? Aren’t they covering for him out of favoritism toward their own?”

“N-no way. There’s absolutely no reason to let a felon—someone who, despite being a representative of the nation, colluded with a foreign power and sparked a war out of personal vendetta—escape. Capturing Nelshen is, you might say, our duty if our country is to survive.”

The men of Shieldfreeden wiped the sweat from their brows as they refuted Father’s words. Well, that’s certainly true. From Shieldfreeden’s perspective, letting him escape would effectively spell the end of their nation, so it’s only natural they’d be frantic to capture him.
“In any case, we plan to conduct our own investigation here in this country, so if we find evidence of collusion, we won’t show any mercy.”
“We’ll take that to heart.”
“We’ll also dispatch some sharp-nosed agents from Siltvelt to track them down, so please rest assured.”

“Ah, either way, they went so far as to engage in covert operations to start a pointless conflict. They’ll have to face the full consequences. Make sure to pinpoint their hideout as soon as possible.”
“‘Yes, sir!’”
Everyone is saluting properly, aren’t they? That’s right. You must show more respect to Father.
“Next… have you identified the group that gave us such a rough welcome, the culprit, and those who aided them?”

“As for the sniper, the Spear Hero immediately neutralized him… and we used the Dragon Hourglass to reset his level. We’re interrogating him in that state. However… it looks like it’ll still take some time.”
“Wouldn’t it be best to cast an illusion that makes him look like Takt on someone capable of using illusion magic?”

Not to mention the first world, but even during the previous loop, Big Sister often used Magic to make me think I was “Filo-chan.” Father looked at me with an expression that said, “That’s pretty ruthless…” But that was just for a moment; he immediately turned to the people from Shieldfreeden and said:
“Ah, that might work on Takt’s subordinates. Something like, ‘Actually, I’m still alive and here to save you! So tell me where my comrades are!’”
“Yes. We plan to use that approach as well. Please wait a moment… though, given the failure of the operation, it’s highly likely the person we targeted has already fled.”
“I suppose so. We had similar results in Siltvelt, after all. What about identifying the informant? Given the amount of explosives they planted, I’d imagine there are quite a few of them.”
“There’s a theory that they weren’t in cahoots with the sniper.”
“Well, it’s possible that different factions were each setting their own traps. Conduct the investigation keeping both possibilities—collaboration and acting independently—in mind.”
“And after we’ve extracted all the information from them, we’ll publicly execute not only the perpetrators but everyone involved in front of the Hero, to make an example of them.”
“Wha…!? O-okay. I suppose that’s a good way to make them realize that further resistance is pointless.”

Father let out a slight gasp. All things considered, he’s actually a kind man. Even in the first world, when public executions were carried out, he watched Takt and the pig-like scum being executed with a look of utter disgust on his face. Apparently, they say that unless we do that, we won’t be setting a proper example. The crime of treating the world like a toy is a grave one, after all. Apparently, if they hadn’t gone through with it, it would have set a bad precedent. Or they would have been condemned for being too lenient.
“As for the explosives, we’ve determined that the components were supervised by Takt.”
“Lasa took them apart—do you know anything about that part?”
Father asks the panda who’s serving as my bodyguard.
“Nope? I only know how to dismantle explosives—I had no idea where they were made. The only thing I can say is that they didn’t place much emphasis on Magic.”
“A factory supervised by Takt, you say… so, is it a Faubrey product?”
“No, it’s a factory built within the territory through a joint venture between Takt—who was close with Nelshen—and others.”

Isn’t that a bit too cozy? Come to think of it, I heard during the last loop that Takt was a cheapskate. In other words, when he does something, he makes the other party foot the bill instead of paying himself.
“So it’s technically a Shieldfreeden product… I took a quick look on the way here, and it looks like there’s a gun shop here, just like in Faubrey.”
“Yes. There’s a factory here that our country, Shieldfreeden, was forced to build on a massive scale under Nelshen’s orders. Would you like to take a look?”
“I suppose so… We should probably figure out just how many engineers of that sort have defected.”

In the first world, it seems that Father has to handle the cases that were resolved by my Finacée, the queen, and Trash. What’s more, it looks like his own role has changed quite a bit—it’s no longer enough to just be in the position of a hero like in the previous loop. I don’t know… I have this nagging feeling that even more trouble is on the horizon.
“Um…”
The people from Shieldfreeden approached Father, their voices hesitant as they gauged his reaction.
“What?”
“Shield Heroes, we would like to ask for your guidance on the direction in which you intend to reform Siltvelt.”
To come all this way and ask what he intends to do now… With a slightly exasperated expression, Father furrowed his brow slightly before letting out a small sigh.

“Our primary objective is the annihilation of the Takt faction. Faubrey put a bounty on them all over the world, but they’ve been too elusive to be wiped out that way. They’re hiding somewhere, growing their ranks like a cult while biding their time. And to think they’d try to seek revenge when the world is already in crisis due to the Waves.”
Father explained to the Shieldfreeden members in a tone of exasperation. Indeed. Considering what lies ahead, we really don’t have the luxury of dealing with Takt’s remnants.
“You know what Takt is accused of, right?”
“Aye!”
The Shieldfreeden members nodded vigorously, indicating they understood that point.

“They treated the world like a toy, yet the survivors—without even grasping the gravity of their crimes—are now scheming to exploit power and profit, or to seek revenge. Honestly, what do you make of that?”
“We recognize it as an unforgivable, grave sin.”

“Right. Eradicating those scum has become our primary objective. Now, the objective that had become secondary by the time we arrived in this country—I came here to confirm it because we must quell the wave of Shieldfreeden. Also—and this overlaps with my primary reason—I came to take action now to ensure we aren’t ambushed in the chaos of participating in the wave or hindered by the people of Shieldfreeden.”

Wow, so there was such a deep reason behind it all. Just as I’d expect from Father. I’m sure the people of Shieldfreeden are filled with gratitude for this as well. Otherwise, I’ll make sure to educate them so that I’ll be the one feeling grateful.
“Well… we appreciate your understanding of the Heroes’ mission.”

“The third objective is to maintain public order in Shieldfreeden, oversee the payment of reparations, and root out those who had been building ties with the Takt faction. Hearing Father present his thoughts—laced with a touch of sarcasm—the people of Shieldfreeden all seemed to understand.
